title: Grateful Dead Live at Universal Amphitheatre on 1973-07-01
lineage: R1 > Technics RS-1506 > TEAC AN-300 [Dolby Decode] > Grace Design Lunatec V3 [Pre-Only] > Korg MR-1000 > DSF [1-bit 5.6448 MHz Stereo] > Korg AudioGate > WAV [24/96]
source: Sony ECM-22P > Sony TC-770 > MAR > ?? [Dolby Encode] > R1

ai_review.summary: Outstanding 1973 audience recording capturing a hot show with smoking Playin', China > Rider, a monster Loose Lucy and superb Jerry Garcia guitar work.
ai_review.review: The tape is an exceptionally clear audience recording for the era, delivering a well‑balanced mix of band and crowd that lets the energy of the night shine through. The performance is high‑octane – highlighted by a colossal Playin', a tight China > Rider sequence, a stellar Loose Lucy and a fiery Jerry Garcia throughout – while Phil’s bass is occasionally buried and the drums sit low in the mix.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high reviewer scores (average 4.6) and enthusiastic comments about both music and sound quality indicate a top‑tier show with excellent recording for its time.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crystal‑clear audience mix with good band balance; occasional mids slightly bright and Phil/drums a bit recessed, but overall superb clarity for a 1973 tape.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Smooth set flow with lively audience banter between songs but never during the music; transitions feel natural and keep the momentum high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia is described as crisp, clear, electrified and on his game throughout the concert.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass sometimes hard to hear and mids a bit high, but other reviewers note Phil sounds good; overall presence is decent.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir gets a positive nod in the metaphorical review, contributing solid rhythm and lead passages.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums are reported as low in the mix and occasionally hard to hear; one reviewer notes Mickey Hart was not playing with them in ’73.
